lines.text: To sell playing cards. And that's not even the weird part.
In Kyoto, a craftsman named Fusajiro Yamauchi started making hand-painted flower cards, called hanafuda.
They became a hit, especially with gamblers, and the little card shop grew.
Decades later, it tried almost anything. A taxi company. Instant rice.
Then it switched to toys, and later, video games.
And here's the weird part. More than a hundred and thirty years later, it still sells those flower cards today.
lines.caption: And here's the weird part. More than 130 years later, it still sells those flower cards today.
